title: Captioning strategy for a huge, repetitive image corpus
prompt: You must generate alt-text captions for billions of images flowing through your pipeline, where a large fraction are exact or near-duplicate copies of images you've already seen. Which captioning strategy do you build around?
constraint: High throughput over a huge corpus with heavy image repetition; per-image cost dominates, and marginal caption-quality gains matter little.

options.why: The constraint says many images repeat and per-image cost dominates — caching by content/perceptual hash collapses redundant work so most images cost a cheap lookup, not a model call. This is the only option whose cost scales with UNIQUE images, not total volume, which is exactly where the savings live.

Defensible: a small model slashes per-call cost versus a large VLM and gives decent captions. But it still pays a model inference for every duplicate, so cost scales with total volume — it ignores the repetition the constraint highlights and leaves the biggest savings on the table.

Highest per-image cost run across the entire corpus including all duplicates — the worst fit for a throughput- and cost-dominated workload. The constraint explicitly says marginal quality gains matter little, so paying premium inference on every repeat is unjustified.

The cache layer is right, but using a large VLM for unique images keeps per-unique-image cost high; at huge scale the long tail of unique images is still enormous, so cost stays dominated by premium inference. The constraint says quality gains matter little, so a small model on misses would be far cheaper for the same goal.
